title: Security questionnaire rapid-response cheat sheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook for responding to customer security questionnaires and Trust Center intake requests related to RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export, and evidence automation.

Scope and intent:
- Target audience: engineering owners, product security, solutions engineers, and CS who draft questionnaire responses for customers and auditors.
- This is a working cheat-sheet not the canonical legal answer. Use for fast turnarounds (SLAs: 24–72h).
- Where a formal artifact is requested (SOC/ISO/pen-test reports), escalate to compliance and legal.

Quick one-line TL;DR answers (copy-paste starters):
- RBAC model: "We use a role-based access control model (RBAC v2) with least-privilege roles and attribute-aware role bindings; role changes are auditable and subject to automated review for privileged roles."
- Audit logging: "All control-plane actions, authentication events, and data-plane administrative operations are logged to an immutable audit stream with tamper-evident retention policies."
- SIEM export: "Audit logs and security events are exportable to customer SIEMs via syslog/S3/HTTPS connectors; field mappings and examples provided on request."
- Evidence automation: "We maintain an evidence workspace that programmatically collects configuration snapshots, access lists, and signed log digests for common questionnaire templates."

Common questionnaire snippets (expand as needed):
1) Describe RBAC and role lifecycle:
- System: RBAC v2 (roles, role-bindings, scoped namespaces).
- Role creation: Requires PR in infra repo + approval from owner + automated lint that checks for admin-scoped privileges.
- Role review cadence: Quarterly automated review for privileged roles; exception tickets required for longer retention.
- Emergency elevation: JIT (just-in-time) temporary elevation via OPA policy + audit trail and automatic expiry.
- Evidence artifacts: role-definitions.csv, recent role-review tickets (JIRA), policy linter output.

2) Audit log schema (practical excerpt):
- Minimal fields we usually provide: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_ip, user_agent, outcome, request_payload_hash, event_signature
- Example single-line JSON (for customer examples):
  {
    "timestamp": "2025-02-05T17:23:44Z",
    "event_id": "evt_01F8X7Y0",
    "actor_id": "user:alice@example.com",
    "action": "role.bind",
    "resource_type": "role",
    "resource_id": "role-admin-prod",
    "outcome": "success"
  }
- Retention: control-plane logs default 1 year; security-critical streams retained 3 years. Configurable per-customer on Dedicated/Private.

3) SIEM export patterns and mapping guidance:
- Accepted export targets: syslog (TLS), HTTPS webhook (JSON), S3 (parquet/ndjson).
- Recommended fields for correlation: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, source_ip, resource_id, action, outcome, trace_id.
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once with sequence tokens; optional exactly-once pipelines available for private deployments via Kafka connector.
- Example mapping note for Splunk: map timestamp->_time, actor_id->user, event_id->transaction_id, request_ip->src_ip.

4) Evidence automation and packaging:
- We run an "evidence-collector" job (internal) that can produce a zip containing: role_definitions.csv, audit_sample.ndjson (30d), config_snapshot.json, signed_digest.txt, and a statement-of-truth.md.
- Automation hooks: GitHub Actions for reproducible snapshots; CI job id and commit hashes included in the package.
- Lead time: automated exports available immediately; curated packages with attestation signed by security take ~3 business days.

Practical response templates (short):
- If asked for fine-grained access control description: paste RBAC one-liner + attach role_definitions.csv and point to Confluence page.
- If asked for logging retention/config: supply retention defaults + note customizable per-customer (Dedicated/Private) + attach sample audit log and schema snippet.
- If asked for SIEM integration: provide connectors list + example mapping file + offer a 1-hour integration workshop with SEs.

Escalation matrix (who to loop in):
- First line: product-security (Priya Kapoor) — technical framing and templates.
- Logs/export technical questions: infra-engineering (Chen Wei).
- RBAC policy/implementation clarifications: serving-runtime (Ravi Patel).
- Legal/compliance sign-off for attestation: Legal – contact via legal@redwood.ai (ticket JIRA-LEGAL-57).

Known gaps / unresolved questions (for follow-up):
- Exact HSM integration wording for Private deployments (need legal-approved phrasing).
- Formal FIPS/KSP validation status on the log-signing component.
- Template for customer-specific SIEM field-mapping (we need to standardize CSV schema).

Attachments to include when preparing an outbound package:
- role_definitions.csv (generated from infra repo)
- audit_schema_v1.3.pdf (short doc with fields and sample events)
- sample_audit_30d.ndjson (redacted)
- evidence_automation_run_manifest.txt (CI job id + commit)
- integration_checklist.md (SE checklist for SIEM onboarding)

Checklist for CS/SE when answering a commercial questionnaire (fast path):
1) Find the exact question (copy into doc).
2) Select the matching TL;DR snippet above.
3) Attach 1–2 supporting artifacts from the list.
4) If customer asks for attested evidence, open JIRA-LEGAL request and add compliance@redwood.ai.
5) Run evidence-collector job if they request logs that are not already packaged.
6) Note any redactions or data masking performed.
7) Add linked artifacts (Confluence, PRs) and send response with offer for integration workshop.

Operational notes for engineers (implementation hints):
- RBAC v2 enforcement is implemented via central policy service backed by a Postgres store and cached in nodes with 5-minute TTL; policy changes publish a change-event we index into the audit stream.
- Log signing uses a per-cluster key rotated quarterly; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM.
- SIEM connectors are implemented as pluggable backends in the logging service; see infra repo PRs for examples (linked above).

Quick copyable entries for Trust Center pages (short):
- "RBAC: Our RBAC v2 provides least-privilege roles, periodic automated reviews, and JIT elevation for emergencies. Role changes are audited and signed."
- "Audit logs: Control and admin events are logged to an immutable stream; customers can export logs to their SIEMs or configure on-prem retention for Private deployments."

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft the standard CSV mapping file for SIEM fields and add to Confluence. (Owner: Chen Wei)
- Confirm exact legal phrase for HSM usage and update templates. (Owner: Priya)
- Create a short demo notebook for SEs showing S3 export -> Splunk ingestion. (Owner: Ravi)

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10 Priya K — initial draft
- 2025-02-18 Chen W — added export targets and mapping notes
- 2025-03-02 Ravi P — added operational hints and example JSON event

End of cheat sheet.
